Shin's Music browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive overdrive browse by type simulation amp simulation browse by enclosure pedal Shin's Music Dumbloid Published on December 5, 2013 Shin's Music amp simulation overdrive pedal Information Shin's Music One of the most iconic and sought after amps in history… in a pedal!  All D*mble amps are different in tone but the main characteristics that set these amps apart are the open uncompressed cleans and the evenly compressed overdrive.  These pedals are very limited.  Shin's music in Tokyo Japan is the builder and he knows tone.  This does not sound like a pedal…it sounds and reacts like an amp.  Many pedals claim this feat but few can back it up…The Dumbloid does! In Jazz mode you can coax tones of many famous players from Robben Ford to Larry Carlton.  The tone get  full, woody, round characteristics.  Kick it in to Rock mode and you get more mids and focus a-la Robben Ford, Keith Urban, Santana.  There is quite a bit of headroom in this pedal it can be used as an organic boost to a full on Overdrive Special! sources.excerpt: Dumbloid Special – Green Hammer by SHIN'S MUSIC | RockBoard | PedalPedia Skip to main content LOG IN EXPLORE SHIN'S MUSIC Dumbloid Special – Green Hammer LOG IN TO SUGGEST IMPROVEMENTS BOOSTER OVERDRIVE Description This premium boutique overdrive stompbox is engineered to replicate the highly sought-after cascading gain characteristics, tactile touch sensitivity, and harmonic richness of rare Dumble Overdrive Special tube amplifiers. The interface features standard drive, tone, and volume controls paired with a specialized accent parameter that shapes the initial pick attack and post-gain presence dynamically. A built-in jazz and rock mini-toggle switch modifies the overall mid-range focus and compression profiles to provide two entirely distinct acoustic characters. The internal analog layout is sealed beneath a thick layer of protective black epoxy resin to hide the specific electronic components from prospective circuit cloners. It is meticulously hand-wired by master builder Shinichi Suzuki in Tokyo, delivering a highly responsive, amp-like saturation profile that scales directly with an instrument's volume adjustments.
